newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon details first wheat purchase of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon details first wheat purchase of 1997.

text.p: Lebanon's economy ministry on Thursday accepted a bid by Beirut-based Loreco, agent for international firm MAPCO, to supply 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this year.
It was the first wheat purchase by Lebanon in 1997.

An official of the Office of Cereals and Sugar Beet said Loreco won the bids to supply the wheat in two shipments of 25,000 tonnes each as it quoted the lowest prices -- $178.75 per tonne for the first batch and $186.90 per tonne for the second.
The first batch is for April 15-May 15 shipment and the second for June 20-July 15 shipment -- both CIF Beirut port silos, the official added.

"Seven companies took part in the tender with prices ranging between $198.15 and $178.75 per tonne for the first shipment and $204.88 and $186.90 per tonne for the second shipment. Loreco supplied the lowest prices and won the bid," the official said.
Last month the economy ministry rejected seven bids for the purchase of 35,000 tonnes of U.S. Hard Red Winter No.2 wheat saying the prices ranging between $203 and $207 per tonne were too high.

The cereals office is part of the economy ministry which periodically invites international firms or their local agents to bid to buy wheat on behalf of the Lebanese government on international markets. The firms also buy wheat for the private sector.
Last year the ministry purchased 200,000 tonnes of wheat through Beirut-based agents of international grain companies.
Lebanon consumes some 400,000 tonnes of wheat a year.
